STEP 1 - Scene: A plated meal with roasted Brussels sprouts, mixed salad leaves, mashed white starch, and three slices of brown meat. It looks like a single main-course plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A white square dinner plate, about 26 cm across. Area ≈ 530 cm². No other plates are part of this meal.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Roasted Brussels sprouts (halved, lightly oiled)
- Mixed salad leaves
- Mashed white starch (potato-like)
- Sliced brown meat (about 3 slices)

STEP 4 - Area (share of plate):
- Brussels sprouts ~10% (53 cm²)
- Salad leaves ~12% (64 cm²)
- Mashed starch ~20% (106 cm²)
- Meat slices ~15% (80 cm²)
- Total ≈ 57% of the plate covered by food, which is plausible.

STEP 5 - Volume (area × height):
- Sprouts: 53 cm² × 2 cm = 106 ml
- Leaves: 64 cm² × 3 cm = 191 ml
- Mash: 106 cm² × 2 cm ≈ 212 ml
- Meat: 80 cm² × 1 cm = 80 ml

STEP 6 - Grams (× bulk density):
- Sprouts: 106 × 0.6 ≈ 64 g
- Leaves: 191 × 0.15 ≈ 29 g
- Mash: 212 × 0.9 ≈ 190 g
- Meat: 80 × 1.0 = 80 g
- Total ≈ 363 g

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Sprouts: 64 g × 50 kcal/100 g ≈ 32 kcal (roasted with a little oil)
- Leaves: 29 g × 20 kcal/100 g ≈ 6 kcal
- Mash: 190 g × 90 kcal/100 g ≈ 171 kcal
- Meat: 80 g × 200 kcal/100 g ≈ 160 kcal
- Total ≈ 369 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 360 g with roughly 370 kcal fits a moderate, visibly half-to-two-thirds-full dinner plate. The mash and meat dominate the energy. The meat identity and the mash type (potato vs. cauliflower) are uncertain, so those kcal values carry the most error.
